source.publication: Instructions for 2025 PIT-ADJ; 2025 PIT-1 Personal Income Tax Return Instructions; 2025 Tax Rate Table (Tax Look Up Table)
source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 7, line 25, Table 2 and Examples 1 and 2; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 99,001.00 + taxable Social Security (85% of gross 60,000.00) 51,000.00 = 150,001.00. Federal taxable income = 150,001.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 2 x 1,600.00 additional for age 65 or older = 115,301.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing jointly. Line 9 federal AGI 150,001.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 34,700.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 150,001.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 55,000.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 13 age 65 or older: Table 1 (married filing jointly) row for federal AGI 150,001.00 gives 0.00 x 2 qualifying = 0.00; line 25 Social Security: federal AGI 150,001.00 exceeds the Table 2 maximum 150,000.00 (married filing jointly), so no part qualifies = 0.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 0.00. Line 17 = 150,001.00 + 0.00 - 34,700.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 115,301.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 115,301.00 = 115,301.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 115,301.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 8,000.00 = 120 + 3.2% x 17,000.00 = 544 + 4.3% x 25,000.00 = 1,075 + 4.7% x 50,000.00 = 2,350 + 4.9% x 15,301.00 = 749.749; total 4,838.749, to the cent 4,838.75. The printed section on T-7 gives 4,836.75; expected keeps the schedule figure 4,838.75, 2.00 more. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 4,838.75.
accepted_approximations: Over 100,000 the printed section is base plus rate, and each base is the table's last row (midpoint 99,950), not the tax at 100,000. A bracket schedule cannot hold that step down, so the schedule gives more than the printed section at every income over 100,000.
